The concept of relativity, specifically time dilation, can be understood through the analogy of a moving walkway at an airport. Imagine you are walking on a moving walkway that is going very fast. To you, your own steps feel normal, and your watch ticks at its usual pace. However, to someone standing still on the ground watching you zoom by, it appears as though you are moving incredibly fast. In the context of relativity, if that walkway were moving close to the speed of light, the person on the ground would see your time passing much more slowly than their own. This happens because time is not a fixed, universal clock but is relative to your speed and the gravitational field you are in. Just as your perception of speed changes based on your frame of reference, your experience of time changes based on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravity is around you.
